reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: Both abiraterone and enzalutamide are well-established agents with known mechanisms - abiraterone inhibits CYP17A1 and enzalutamide antagonizes androgen receptor. Standard dosing was used (1000mg and 160mg daily respectively), suggesting adequate target engagement likely occurred. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No biomarker data provided to confirm androgen pathway suppression, but these are established agents with known pharmacodynamic effects. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint was not met. Group A (combination) had 13 participants with ≤ypT2N0 vs Group B (abiraterone alone) with 11 participants - minimal difference suggesting no meaningful clinical benefit from adding enzalutamide. No p-value reported but effect size appears negligible. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: Small sample size (n=69) may have been underpowered to detect differences. Multiple serious safety signals including pancreatitis, stroke, and pulmonary embolism suggest tolerability issues that could have impacted dosing or compliance.
